lead: North Las Vegas plumbing deals with very hard water, desert heat and mostly newer slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across North Las Vegas.
risk: very hard water scale, water heater wear and slab leaks
risk_short: hard water, water heaters and slab leaks
why: The southern part of the city, near Downtown North Las Vegas, has homes from the 1950s to the 1970s with galvanized lines and cast-iron drains. Aliante, Eldorado and Tule Springs were built mostly after 2000.
Homes sit on slabs, so leaks under the floor happen. Very hard water and hot garages wear out water heaters.
utility: City of North Las Vegas Utilities
water: North Las Vegas gets its water from Lake Mead through the Southern Nevada Water Authority. It is very hard, so scale builds up fast in heaters, tankless units and fixtures.
tips: Flush your water heater every year.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
Follow local watering rules; leaks are costly.
areas: PipeMend works in Aliante, Eldorado, Craig Ranch, Valley Vista, Tule Springs, Downtown North Las Vegas and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of North Las Vegas Building Safety Division, and contractors must be licensed by the Nevada State Contractors Board.

faq.q: Do North Las Vegas homes need water softeners?
faq.a: Many owners add one. The water from Lake Mead is very hard, and scale shortens the life of water heaters and fixtures. A water test helps size a softener.
